ASRC Federal System Solutions is seeking a Licensed Electrician / Installation Technician to support the FAA’s Radar System Replacement (RSR) program, the largest and most significant radar modernization effort within the National Airspace System (NAS). This role will provide licensed electrical expertise in support of the installation, power integration, grounding, and startup of cooperative, non-cooperative, and integrated surveillance systems at FAA facilities nationwide.
Work location: Remote, travel required. Clearance: Public Trust. US Citizenship to successfully complete a government investigation.
Summary This position is central to ensuring that all electrical installation activities are performed safely, correctly, and in compliance with applicable codes, standards, and FAA requirements. The Licensed Electrician will execute and oversee electrical work associated with radar equipment power distribution, grounding and earthing systems, surge protection devices, and coordination with FAA facility power infrastructure.
The Engineering / Installation Technician (Licensed Electrician) will work closely with construction managers, system engineers, and installation teams to support successful installation, testing, and acceptance of radar systems under a compressed, nationwide deployment schedule.

Perform licensed electrical installation activities supporting radar room equipment, antenna systems, and associated infrastructure.
Install, terminate, and test power cabling for radar, communications, and support equipment in accordance with approved designs and electrical codes.
Coordinate with FAA facility personnel for connection into site power switchboards and electrical distribution systems.
Install and connect grounding and earthing systems, including busbars, grounding conductors, and Surge Protective Devices (SPDs).
Support power connection testing, verification, and documentation required for system energization.
Assist with electrical aspects of antenna installations, including power, grounding, and lightning protection interfaces.
Support installation acceptance testing (IAT) and system start-up activities related to electrical and power subsystems.
Identify, troubleshoot, and resolve electrical installation issues encountered during field activities.
Prepare required electrical installation documentation, reports, and as-built information.
Ensure all electrical work complies with safety, security, quality, and FAA operational requirements.

High school diploma or equivalent; completion of an accredited electrical apprenticeship or trade program required.
2-4 years with demonstrated experience performing commercial or industrial electrical work.
Must have active licensed electrician certification (state or jurisdictional license)
Hands-on experience with power distribution systems, electrical panels, grounding, bonding, and surge protection.
Experience installing and terminating electrical cabling for technical or mission-critical systems.
Strong knowledge of applicable electrical codes and standards (e.g., NEC, NFPA, local codes).
Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, schematics, and installation documentation.
Experience working in operational or safety-critical environments with strict compliance requirements.
Willingness and ability to travel to FAA sites nationwide.
Physical ability to perform field electrical work, including lifting, climbing, and working in confined spaces.
US Citizenship to successfully complete a government investigation.

Experience supporting FAA facilities, air traffic management systems, or federal infrastructure programs.
Prior electrical installation experience on radar systems, communications systems, or other high-reliability technical installations.
Experience with grounding, lightning protection systems, and SPDs at exposed or elevated sites.
Familiarity with radar room environments, equipment racks, and mission-critical power systems.
OSHA safety certification or equivalent electrical safety training.
Experience supporting multi-site deployment programs with parallel installation schedules.

Installs, alters, maintains and repairs electrical facilities and equipment

## **Ta mission :** ##
**Réaliser des projets de rénovation électrique complets**
Vous intervenez sur des chantiers de rénovation d-appartements, de villas et de bâtiments résidentiels, en assurant la modernisation, la mise aux normes et la fiabilisation des installations électriques.
**Lire et interpréter les documents techniques**
Vous analysez les plans et schémas électriques afin de garantir une exécution précise, conforme aux exigences du projet et aux normes en vigueur.
**Effectuer les travaux de préparation et de câblage**
Vous réalisez les travaux de saignées à l-aide de rainureuse, le gainage ainsi que le tirage de câbles nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des installations électriques.
**Installer et raccorder les équipements électriques**
Vous assurez la pose, le raccordement et la mise en service des appareillages, tableaux électriques, luminaires et autres équipements, dans le respect des normes et standards de qualité.
**Intervenir sur les installations CFO/CFA**
Vous participez à l-installation, la modification et la mise en service de systèmes en courant fort et courant faible, en garantissant leur fiabilité, leur performance et leur sécurité.
**Assurer le dépannage et les adaptations techniques**
Vous diagnostiquez les dysfonctionnements, réalisez les interventions de dépannage et effectuez les transformations nécessaires sur les installations existantes.
**Travailler en autonomie et représenter l-entreprise**
En contact direct avec les clients sur le terrain, vous faites preuve de professionnalisme, de rigueur et d-un excellent sens du service afin de garantir leur satisfaction tout au long des interventions
## **Maintenant si on parlait de toi ?** ##
**Une formation solide dans le domaine électrique**
Vous êtes titulaire d-un CFC de monteur-électricien ou d-une formation équivalente reconnue. Vous disposez des compétences techniques nécessaires pour intervenir de manière autonome sur des projets de rénovation électrique.
**Une expérience confirmée en rénovation**
Vous justifiez de plusieurs années d-expérience dans la rénovation de villas, appartements et bâtiments résidentiels. Vous maîtrisez les travaux de transformation, de modernisation et de mise en conformité des installations électriques.
**Une réelle autonomie sur le terrain**
Habitué à gérer vos chantiers de manière indépendante, vous savez organiser votre travail, prendre des initiatives et assurer un suivi rigoureux des interventions qui vous sont confiées.
**Un excellent savoir-être**
Grâce à votre sens du service, votre professionnalisme et votre présentation soignée, vous représentez l-entreprise de manière fiable et sérieuse auprès des clients et des différents intervenants sur les chantiers.
**Des connaissances techniques appréciées**
La maîtrise des normes NIBT constitue un véritable atout et vous permet d-intervenir dans le respect des exigences de sécurité et de qualité en vigueur.
**Mobilité et disponibilité**
Titulaire du permis de conduire, vous êtes à l-aise avec les déplacements quotidiens sur différents chantiers. Une disponibilité rapide est fortement appréciée afin de rejoindre les équipes dans les meilleurs délais.
**Un profil fiable et engagé**

Frequently lifts parts and equipment that weigh up to 20 pounds unassisted, and occasionally up to 50 pounds with assistance of lifting devices or other workers.

Working Conditions: Works in hangars and on flight lines. Subject to drafts, noise, and varying temperatures in hangars and weather, temperature, and noise extremes on flight lines. Exposed to dust, dirt, grease, oil, fumes, solvents, and other aircraft fluids while working on aircraft in various stages of repair or modification.

Exposed to the possibility of abrasions, cuts, burns, electrical shock, skin and eye irritation, and falls from elevated work areas, e.g., check stands and aircraft structures. May be subject to exposure to potential injury from turning rotors or jet blast during engine runups.

PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week.

VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

All MWEOC staff have emergency assignments and are considered deployed in place. Exercises and activations are planned and unplanned, and may require long hours, nights, weekends and holidays.

All MWEOC employees are: (1) required to use a government-issued electronic device (to include cellular phones); (2) subject to recall during emergency situations; and (3) required to perform work in locations both above and below ground. What will I do in this position if hired?

In this position, you will serve as a High Voltage Electrician Supervisor responsible for supervising in the maintenance, repair, and modification of low and high voltage electrical systems and equipment. As senior electrician, you will also be responsible for electrical maintenance, installation, testing, troubleshooting and repair.

Typical assignments include: Troubleshooting and repair of electrical wiring systems and associated fixtures, controls, equipment in industrial, commercial office, and residential buildings. Traces and repairs hard to locate defects or problems. Repairs or replaces a wide variety of electrical equipment.

Reading building plans, blueprints, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings, and electrical maintenance and repair manuals to install electrical lines, circuits, systems, equipment and controls.

Installing various types of conduits with associated couplings, connectors, and straps, to include electrical metallic tubing (EMT), rigid, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), liquid tight flexible conduit, and wire mold (pulling and terminating wire in all of the above); wiring and installing service distribution panels and disconnects, transformers, switches and receptacles.

Interpreting and applying the National Electrical Code, local codes, building plans, and uses formulas to calculate common properties. i.e. ohms law. What else do I need to know? At FEMA, our mission is to help people before, during and after disasters, and every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management.

Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites.

All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description.

Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions.
The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of this announcement. Ability to Lead or Supervise Ability to supervise or lead electricians performing common tasks for low and high voltage electrical systems and equipment; plan, coordinate, and assign work to provide technical direction or help.

Able to install, modify, repair, maintain, troubleshoot, and test electrical lines, circuits, systems and equipment. Use working knowledge or ability under close supervision of a work leader using building plans, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings to plan and layout routing of electrical equipment.

Applicants will be rated in accordance with the OPM Federal Wage System Qualification Standard.

Although a specific length of time and experience is not required for most trade and labor occupations, you must meet any screen-out element listed, and show through experience and training that you possess the quality level of knowledge and skill necessary to perform the duties of the position at the level for which you are applying.

Qualification requirements emphasis is on the quality of experience, not necessarily the length of time. Working Conditions: The work is performed both inside and outside.

Electrical workers are sometimes required to make repairs and installations in bad weather; in work areas that are noisy, dirty, dusty, and greasy; on scaffolding or cranes at heights of 9 meters (30 feet) or more; and in close quarters such as manholes, or attics.

They are occasionally exposed to the possibility of injury from falling, electrical shock, burns, and rotary devices such as electrical motors. They are frequently exposed to the possibility of cuts and bruises.

They are exposed to danger from explosions of equipment and cables in manholes and vaults, as well as danger from high voltage electrical shock, burns from solder, broken bones, cuts, and bruises.

They are exposed to heat and noise when working in substationsor power-generating facilities, to extremes of weather when working outdoors, and to unpleasant odors and wet slippery surfaces when working in manholes.

They are subject to electrical burns while working around high voltage electrical lines, broken bones fromfalls from poles, and strains from awkward work positions. They are exposed to chemicals such as insulation oil from transformers and oil switches. They use protective devices such as earplugs, safety hats, and nonconductive gloves and footwear.

Physical Effort: Workers frequently perform moderately heavy lifting, pulling, and carrying of equipment and material weighing up to 18 kilograms (40 pounds) and occasionally, they lift or pull heavy cables and equipment weighing more than 23 kilograms ( 50 pounds) with the help of weight handling equipment or with assistance from other workers.

They use block and tackle, pulleys, or other lifting devices. They crouch, stand, kneel, and stoop while installing, repairing, or testing electrical equipment in confined spaces such as enclosed switch gear, or in structures such as overhead bus and conduit assemblies.

Workers work above ground from aerial bucket trucks and poles, at ground level, and in trenches, or manholes. Work requires bending, stooping, climbing, and standing for long periods while installing, repairing, and testing electrical equipment in manholes and on overhead distribution lines in tiring and uncomfortable positions.

Electrical workers make repairs and installations from ladders, scaffolding, platforms, and other hard-to-reach places.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. NOTE: Qualifications are based on breadth/level of experience.
